title: Who and What Questions - One Table
description: Put {qui est-ce qui}, {qui est-ce que}, {qu'est-ce qui} and {qu'est-ce que} in one table.
can_do: Ask who or what does something: {Qui est-ce qui parle ?}, {Qu'est-ce qui tombe ?}
Ask who or what someone sees or wants: {Qui est-ce que tu vois ?}, {Qu'est-ce que tu veux ?}
line: The first word asks about a person or a thing, and the last word says whether it does the action or receives it.

parts.heading: Four questions, one table
text: Each question has two halves. The start, {qui} or {qu'}, asks about a person or a thing. The end, {qui} or {que}, says whether that person or thing does the action or receives it.

parts.heading: The start: a person or a thing
text: {qui} at the start asks about a person. {qu'} at the start asks about a thing.

pairs: Qui est-ce qui est à gauche ?

parts.heading: The end: does it or receives it
text: {qui} at the end means the person or thing does the action, so the verb usually comes next. {que} at the end means it receives the action, so another subject comes next, such as {tu}.

parts.heading: All four in use
text: Read the start for a person or a thing, then the end for who does the action.

lines: Qui est-ce qui tourne à droite ?
Qui est-ce que tu vois au coin de la rue ?
Who do you see on the street corner?
Qu'est-ce qui rend la ville moderne ?
Qu'est-ce que les habitants font le soir ?
What do the locals do in the evening?

checks.why: A thing is falling, so the question starts with {qu'}, and the thing does the action, so it ends with {qui}: {qu'est-ce qui}.

checks.ask: Which one asks “Who do you see?”
checks.why: You ask about a person, so it starts with {qui}. The person is the one seen, and {tu} comes next, so it ends with {que}.

checks.ask: Listen. Does this ask about a person or a thing?
checks.why: It starts with {qu'}, so it asks about a thing: what you are eating.
